Three Days in Kyoto: Temples, Ramen, and Falling Leaves

Kyoto takes time to get to know, and three days is enough to see why people go back.

My first morning began at 6 a.m. at Fushimi Inari. Mist still clung to the hillside, and the thousands of vermilion torii gates glowed in the early light. A few other early risers were on the path, so the climb felt almost private. I heard birdsong and the crunch of gravel underfoot.

By midday I was hungry, and I found a tiny counter near Kyoto Station. A 900 yen bowl of ramen arrived with rich broth, springy noodles, and tender chashu. For that price it was hard to beat.

Then I walked the Philosopher's Path in autumn, along a canal under maples gone red and gold. Leaves drifted onto the water.

The rest of this guide lays out the three days in order, from sunrise shrines to slow afternoon walks.
